newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan students say police disperse protesters.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan students say police disperse protesters.

text.p: Moroccan authorities deployed security forces at a Casablanca university on Friday to disperse students protesting against the trial of three students from an outlawed Moslem fundamentalist group.
One student, who asked not to be named, said around ten security force vehicles were sent to the Hassan II university to break up the protest.

The three students, who went on trial on Thursday, face up to two years in prison if found guilty of the charge of "disturbing order and aggression against a civil servant", defence lawyer Mustafa Ramid said.

The three belonged to the outlawed fundamentalist al-Adl wal Ihsane (Justice and Charity) group and students said they were arrested recently in Casablanca after unrest in the campus over transport problems.
Morocco's official news agency MAP said on Friday that Interior Minister Driss Basri and top security officials met the previous day to discuss the situation in the universities.

MAP said university officials briefed the gathering on the "action led by minority groups, generally not connected with the establishments concerned, aimed at disrupting by illegal means the normal course of studies."
The court was expected to issue its decision on the three students on Tuesday. Twenty-seven other students would appear in court on Monday charged with similar offences.
The lawyer said around 50 more students were arrested on Thursday at Ain Chock university in Casablanca.
A student union spokesman told Reuters by telephone from Casablanca that police had arrested 54 people on Friday at several universities.
Officials at the interior ministry were not immediately available for comment.
